chapter: Arranging, Fletcher Henderson and Lucky Millinder
title: Stuffy solo as his identity in 1945, and Ladies Lullaby
summary: Thompson hums the solo that first identified him as a jazz soloist, around 1945, and says he wrote originals for the band including Ladies Lullaby for Billie Holiday.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: -- that they had played until his death. My solo went like this. (Humming).
And the first time I was able to establish my identity as a jazz player as a soloist, believe it or not. And that was I think 1945.
Then I later on went from there and I wrote a lot of original songs for the band. I had many -- one called 'Ladies Lullaby', which I wrote as a dedication to Lady Day, Billie Holiday.
And some other things that I did with the band.
Did that get any lyrics, 'Ladies Lullaby'?
No, no, it never got even popular.
